company.text: Seviroli started as a **pastry shop in Queens in 1960** and grew into a family-owned frozen pasta maker (ravioli, tortellini, stuffed shells, manicotti, short cuts) plus a specialty Italian import line (**Vertullo**, 150+ items from 19 countries). **Mill Point Capital** bought it in **Dec 2022** (financing by PGIM). Since then it has been a roll-up: **Mama Rosie's** (Boston, founded 1976) in **Jul 2023**, and the **Bernardi, Rotanelli's and Mona's** Italian frozen pasta brands from **Ajinomoto Foods North America** in **Jan 2024**. It also owns **D'Orazio**. In **2025** it closed its Bellmawr, NJ plant (77 jobs) and moved production to **Garden City and Hauppauge, NY**. The brands are now unified under **Fresia Foods** ("Premium Pastas. For Every Chef."), which claims the **world's largest tortellini operation** and stresses **private label** for retailers and **foodservice**. Channels: foodservice, club and grocery/retail (e.g. Mama Rosie's at Stop & Shop). CEO in 2023: **Paul Vertullo** (to be confirmed if still in role).

financials.text: No public revenue. Third-party estimate: **~$50M revenue**, **101–200 employees** (Prospeo; figures conflict, treat as rough). Likely higher after the Ajinomoto and Mama Rosie's deals — **to be confirmed**. Debt-financed by PGIM (revolver, term loan, sub notes). PE ownership usually means a focus on **cost savings and margin** — a good angle for supplier consolidation.

industry.title: Frozen is big and moving to value
industry.text: US frozen food is a **$93.5B** market. Value-size packs are **40%+** of frozen aisle sales; "takeout-style" frozen is **$14.3B** (Conagra Future of Frozen Food 2026). Restaurant-quality Italian at home fits Fresia's pitch.

industry.title: The freezer door is the battleground
industry.text: Shoppers decide at the shelf, and frozen is hard to merchandise: closed doors, cold surfaces, little space. Door clings, shelf talkers, secondary displays and digital screens are the levers. Industry claims of **~70% of decisions made at shelf** are unverified — use as directional only.

industry.title: Private label pressure
industry.text: Fresia leans into **private label** for retailers. That means its own brands (Mama Rosie's, Seviroli) must earn shelf space with stronger in-store support.

talking_points: What is in your 2027 plan for retail versus foodservice and private label?
With four brands now under Fresia, how are you rolling out the new identity — sell sheets, trade shows, in-store?
How many print, display and promo suppliers do you work with today across the brands?
How do you support Mama Rosie's and Seviroli at shelf today — freezer door, endcaps, demos?
Which retailers or club accounts are priorities for 2027?
How do you measure whether in-store materials actually get installed?
Are you exhibiting at AFFI-CON or other shows in 2027? Who builds your booth?
Who else is involved in budget decisions — procurement, CEO, Mill Point?
